Tariq: Heads-up — customer Vela reported a regression after we merged their LoRA into the public adapter build and quantized to 4-bit. Quick numbers from a light smoke run: EM dropped ~6.9% vs baseline.

Tariq: Command I ran:
```
./tools/run_eval --model redwood/vela:merged-lora:quant4 --evalset s3://vela-evals/qasets/qaset_v1.json --batch 8 --output /tmp/vela-smoke.json
```

eval-bot: automated summary: run_id=vela-smoke-1979012345, EM=72.1 (baseline 79.0), F1=80.3 (baseline 86.5), avg_latency=48ms (+8ms), samples=250

Eva: yikes. Can you repro locally with FP16 merged binary (no quant) to see if merge or quant caused it? Also include the merge ref/command and adapter config. :eyes:

Tariq: I did a quick FP16 pass earlier — FP16 merged was ~78.6 EM so much closer. That points at quant path. Merge used: `adapter-merge --base redwood/vela-base:1.4 --adapter vela-lora-2026-03 --method=merge-with-rescale --alpha=0.75`

Sasha: @Tariq thanks. Two hypotheses: 1) quant rounding hitting layernorm/bias folding, 2) merge alpha not preserved correctly in quant kernels. Also check if the KV cache dtype promoted somewhere.

Matt: can you paste a tiny logits diff for a couple of examples? If quant changes first-token logits significantly that'd explain EM drop.

Tariq: minimal diff script I used:
```python
# logs/diff_logits.py
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np

ref = np.load('ref_logits.npy')   # fp16 merged
q = np.load('q_logits.npy')       # quant4 merged
kl = np.sum(ref * (np.log(ref+1e-9) - np.log(q+1e-9)), axis=-1)
print('mean token KL', kl.mean())
print('top tokens', np.argsort(kl)[-5:])
```

Tariq: Run results: mean token KL=0.42 on the first 128 tokens sample. Top KL concentrated in first 6 tokens (greeting / system prompt region).

Eva: that smells like a tokenization/embedding alignment or quantized embedding layer mismatch. Did the quantizer treat the embedding table differently (per-channel vs per-tensor)?

Sasha: Good call. If embedding was per-tensor vs per-channel we can lose distribution fidelity. Also check if adapter merge was applied post-quantization accidentally in the build pipeline.

Tariq: Build log snippet: `build: apply-quantize -> apply-adapter` — oh. That is the issue: our pipeline quantized base model, then applied adapter merge on quantized weights. That would fold adapter weights poorly.

Matt: ok that's actionable. Short-term fix: re-run pipeline so merge happens before quantization, then apply per-channel quant to embeddings and use a calibration pass. I can make a Canary job.

Eva: I'll assemble a "vela-quick-eval" pack focusing on QA and a small set of prompts that capture the dropped cases and push to s3: `s3://redwood-smoke-packs/vela/quickpack_v1.jsonl`. We'll include 50 targeted prompts + 200 random QA.

Sasha: Also add a small KL-check harness to the eval pack so CI can block merges that increase mean token KL > 0.15 on the targeted set.

Tariq: working on re-merging with merge-before-quant and alpha=0.9, then do per-channel quant on embeddings + calibration. I'll post the run_id when done.

eval-bot: created canary job vela-canary-1979012600 with policy: run FP16 merged + quant4 merged (merge-before-quant) on quickpack_v1, store outputs -> s3://redwood-smoke-outputs/vela/1979012345-canary.json

Eva: plan: keep FP16 merged variant on Dedicated for customer until we validate quant build. If canary looks good (EM delta < 1.5 and token KL < 0.15) we promote. Otherwise rollback quantized revision. :thumbsup:

Tariq: Thanks team — I'll update once canary completes (should be ~20m).
